A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SASHA study and contain 23 readable pages, including Appendices A.1–A.6. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of the text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v3 reports original classification experiments on four datasets, component ablations, sampling analyses, and computational measurements, including Tables 1–2 and 9–13.

after.justification: v4 retains these original classification experiments, ablations, sampling analyses, and computational measurements in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: SASHA's HAFED feature distiller, targeted state updater, PPO training, and deterministic inference are unchanged in Section 3, Algorithm 1, and Appendix A.2.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same CAMELYON16 and TCGA-NSCLC binary tasks and Camelyon+ and BRACS multiclass tasks. No dataset or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the main and appendix comparisons, including RLogist, Zoom-MIL, ACMIL, and DTFD. The same alternative sampling policies and reward schedules are compared.

E3.justification: Data splits, preprocessing, observation budgets, metrics, model configurations, and training and evaluation procedures remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices A.1–A.4.

E4.justification: The component ablations, limited-budget comparisons, inference-policy and reward-schedule controls, and agent-behavior analyses are identical in Section 4 and Appendix A.3.

E5.justification: Table 10 retains means and standard deviations across five splits and three sampling seeds per split. Significance annotations in Figure 3 and standard-deviation bands in Figure 4 are also unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings match. For example, Table 1 retains SASHA-0.2 CAMELYON16 accuracy of 0.953 ± 0.017 and AUC of 0.979 ± 0.008; appendix results and plotted findings are also identical.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and reasoning are unchanged, including the state-update formulation, cumulative tumor-patch hit ratio in Equation 1, and compressibility formula in Appendix A.4.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about selective sampling, diagnostic performance, computational efficiency, and memory savings.

C2.justification: Interpretations of sampling behavior and calibration remain identical. Section 5 and Appendix A.6 retain the same training-cost, fixed-budget, architecture-overhead, sparse-tumor, and clinical-applicability discussion.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware disclosures, and the model-code access statement are unchanged in Appendix A.2, Appendix A.5, and the page 1 footnote.

R1.justification: Section 2, citations throughout the paper, and the 41-entry bibliography are unchanged. No research-positioning or novelty statement is revised.

P1.justification: v4 adds the Gore Subraya Bhat Chair Associate Professorship in Digital Health to the support acknowledged on page 10 and updates the arXiv version/date stamp on page 1. Scientific prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–5, Tables 1–13, captions, and placement are identical. The acknowledgement edit only rewraps text within its existing block; the surrounding page layout remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 adds a support acknowledgement but leaves the methods, evidence, explanations, reproducibility information, and limitations unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. This administrative clarification produces no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
